Hey! I’m Rayane, a 1st-year Aerospace student at UIR ,passionate about space tech, systems design, and AI.  

Driven by a strong UIR x UM6P collaboration, our team is tackling the "Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars" challenge.
summary:
How can we prepare for life on the Moon and Mars without first understanding the worlds beneath our feet?

NEXORA SPACE - ECHO-VOID ATLAS is an interactive planetary exploration platform that transforms Earth into a testing ground for future space missions. Addressing NASA's challenge to identify terrestrial analogs for lunar and Martian environments, we connect five diverse Earth locations with Jezero Crater on Mars and the lunar south pole.

Combining NASA elevation data, geospatial analysis, and interactive visualization, NEXORA investigates terrain slope, roughness, relief, and data reliability. Through EXPLORE, users discover candidate sites; ANALYZE reveals measurable similarities and scientific limitations; and ECHO, our 3D drone simulator, demonstrates virtual terrain reconnaissance.

Our innovation is evidence-first exploration: when data is insufficient, NEXORA reveals uncertainty rather than inventing similarity scores.

By connecting real planetary science with immersive simulation, NEXORA makes analog-site research accessible to students, researchers, and future explorers-helping turn Earth's landscapes into stepping stones toward responsible exploration beyond our planet.
details:
NEXORA SPACE - ECHO-VOID ATLAS

Explore Earth. Understand other worlds. Plan with evidence.

1. The Problem: Where on Earth Can We Prepare for Other Worlds?

Before establishing permanent infrastructure on the Moon or expanding human exploration of Mars, scientists and engineers need environments where they can investigate terrain, test exploration concepts, and prepare future missions.

Earth contains extraordinary planetary analog candidates: arid deserts, volcanic landscapes, impact craters, and polar regions. Yet a location that visually resembles Mars or the Moon may differ significantly in terrain characteristics and environmental conditions.

The challenge is not simply finding places that look extraterrestrial. It is determining which similarities are supported by scientific evidence.

NEXORA SPACE was developed to address this problem by connecting Earth observation, planetary topography, and simulated field reconnaissance within a single interactive platform.

2. Our Solution: Explore, Analyze, Recon

NEXORA SPACE - ECHO-VOID ATLAS is a web-based planetary analog investigation platform designed around three interconnected experiences.

EXPLORE - Discover Terrestrial Analogs

Our interactive geographic explorer introduces five Earth locations selected for their diverse environmental characteristics:

  • Erfoud, Morocco: Arid desert landscapes and geomorphology.
  • Atacama Desert, Chile: Extreme aridity and rugged terrain.
  • Askja, Iceland: Volcanic landscapes and geological exploration.
  • Haughton Crater, Canada: Impact-related geology and Arctic environments.
  • McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica: Cold-desert terrain and polar exploration conditions.

Users select an Earth candidate and investigate its relevance to Jezero Crater on Mars or the lunar south pole.

These sites are treated as potential analog environments, not automatically validated equivalents of planetary locations.

ANALYZE - Compare Terrain Using Scientific Data

NEXORA combines terrestrial elevation datasets with NASA planetary observations to investigate measurable terrain properties.

Our Python-based geospatial pipeline calculates:

  • Mean slope: The average steepness of terrain.
  • 90th-percentile slope: A measure of steeper terrain conditions.
  • Surface roughness: Local variations in elevation.
  • Relief: The elevation range within the study area.

These measurements provide an initial foundation for evaluating terrain morphology.

The analysis also considers geographic coverage, data resolution, observation support, and processing uncertainty.

What makes our approach distinctive is that we do not present missing scientific evidence as certainty. When a comparison fails the required validation checks, NEXORA marks it as provisional and withholds an unsupported similarity score.

RECON - Meet ECHO, Our Virtual Reconnaissance Drone

ECHO is an interactive 3D drone simulator developed to explore how robotic reconnaissance could support terrestrial analog investigations.

Built using Three.js, ECHO allows users to explore a virtual terrain environment, conduct simulated survey missions, monitor mission progress, and visualize reconnaissance coverage.

Its mission model includes flight controls, survey planning, and simulated operational constraints.

ECHO does not claim to collect real satellite measurements or represent a flight-ready lunar drone. It is a virtual representation of Earth-based robotic reconnaissance, designed to connect terrain analysis with exploration planning.

REPORT - Turn Exploration into Traceable Results

The reporting experience brings together the selected Earth site, planetary target, available terrain evidence, data-quality limitations, and simulated mission information.

Structured outputs support reproducibility and allow users to distinguish scientific observations from simulation results.

3. Scientific Methodology: From Raw Elevation Data to Evidence

Our methodology follows six stages.

Stage 1 - Analog Site Selection

We investigate five terrestrial regions representing different geological and environmental conditions and associate them with two planetary study targets.

Stage 2 -Data Acquisition

Our initial scientific comparisons use NASA NASADEM terrestrial elevation data and Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) datasets from NASA's Planetary Data System.

Additional elevation sources identified for broader investigations include Copernicus DEM, ArcticDEM, REMA, and lunar LOLA products.

Stage 3 - Spatial Normalization

Because Earth and planetary datasets differ in projection, resolution, and reference systems, our processing workflow establishes geographic study windows and comparable analysis grids.

Initial Earth–Mars terrain comparisons use approximately 32 km × 32 km study areas analyzed at a documented 1 km working resolution.

Stage 4 - Terrain Characterization

The pipeline derives slope, roughness, and relief metrics from the available elevation grids.

Measurements are interpreted at the working analysis scale rather than being treated as direct evidence of fine-scale surface conditions.

Stage 5 - Scientific Quality Assessment

We evaluate the reliability of the underlying elevation observations.

For our Jezero Crater study window, analysis of the MOLA observation-count product showed that approximately 38.8% of inspected native grid cells contained at least one direct laser observation.

This revealed an important distinction: a continuous-looking elevation map does not necessarily represent continuous direct measurement.

We therefore document observational limitations and avoid presenting interpolated terrain as fully observed.

Stage 6 - Explainable Comparison and Reconnaissance

The platform presents available terrain metrics alongside scientific limitations, then enables a separate ECHO reconnaissance simulation.

Our initial Erfoud–Jezero and Atacama–Jezero analyses remain explicitly provisional. Other site combinations are part of the broader investigation framework and require further processing or validation.


4. What Makes NEXORA Creative?

Our innovation lies in connecting scientific analysis with an immersive exploration workflow while keeping scientific uncertainty visible.

Evidence before confidence: Unlike platforms that produce unexplained similarity percentages, NEXORA is designed to withhold a numerical conclusion when the evidence is insufficient.

A cross-world perspective: Users can investigate multiple terrestrial environments in relation to both Mars and lunar exploration objectives.

Interactive reconnaissance: ECHO transforms abstract mission-planning concepts into a 3D experience where users can explore virtual survey operations.

Transparent scientific communication: The analysis identifies where measurements originate, what they describe, and where their limitations begin.

Accessible planetary science: NEXORA makes geospatial concepts and the role of terrestrial analogs understandable beyond specialist research environments.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

NEXORA SPACE aims to support three groups.

Researchers and engineering students can explore preliminary terrain-comparison methods and understand the limitations of transferring Earth-based observations to planetary mission contexts.

Educators and learners can investigate remote sensing, terrain morphology, scientific uncertainty, and robotic reconnaissance through an interactive application.

Future mission designers can use the platform as an educational starting point for discussing analog-site investigation and the additional evidence needed for realistic field-testing campaigns.

Our long-term vision is to develop NEXORA into an open, evidence-aware planetary analog investigation environment that can incorporate broader terrain observations, thermal data, geological information, and actual field-reconnaissance measurements.

6. Technologies and Tools

NEXORA combines web development, scientific programming, geospatial processing, and 3D simulation.

Frontend

  • React - Interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript - Type-safe application development.
  • Vite - Development and production build system.
  • Leaflet - Geographic exploration and interactive maps.
  • Three.js - ECHO 3D reconnaissance simulation.

Scientific and Geospatial Processing

  • Python - Scientific processing and validation.
  • NumPy - Numerical terrain calculations.
  • Rasterio - Geospatial raster processing.
  • JSON Schema - Validation of structured scientific outputs.

Development and Collaboration

  • Git and GitHub - Version control and collaboration.
  • Automated tests - Validation of frontend behavior, geospatial processing, and scientific-data rules.

Scientific Data

  • NASADEM - Terrestrial elevation.
  • MOLA - Martian topography and observation counts.
  • Copernicus DEM, ArcticDEM, and REMA - Additional terrestrial elevation sources identified for expanded analysis.
  • LOLA - Lunar topography source identified for future lunar comparison validation.

7. Factors Our Team Considered

We made several important design decisions throughout development.

Scientific validity: Elevation-derived terrain similarity must not be confused with geological, thermal, or operational equivalence.

Data reliability: We document missing observations, interpolation, spatial resolution, and the impact of processing methods.

Reproducibility: The analysis uses structured scientific outputs and a testable processing pipeline.

Responsible simulation: Virtual flight behavior and survey coverage are identified as simulated rather than measured data.

Accessibility: The interface connects specialized planetary science concepts to an intuitive exploration workflow.

Performance: Scientific data can be processed separately from the web application so users can explore results without downloading extremely large elevation archives.

8. Limitations and Future Development

NEXORA is an exploratory prototype rather than a certified system for selecting planetary landing sites or establishing permanent bases.

Our current comparisons are preliminary. Elevation alone cannot establish subsurface resources, mineral composition, temperature, radiation exposure, ground strength, illumination, or overall habitat suitability.

Future work includes completing additional Earth–Mars and Earth–Moon comparisons, incorporating validated LOLA and Diviner observations, adding environmental and geological measurements, and linking ECHO more closely to verified site-specific terrain.

We intentionally distinguish what has been measured, what has been simulated, and what still requires investigation.

9. Our Vision

The road to the Moon and Mars begins on Earth-but only if we understand what Earth's landscapes can actually teach us.

NEXORA SPACE transforms open scientific data into an interactive environment where anyone can explore planetary analog candidates, understand the evidence behind terrain comparisons, and experience the principles of robotic reconnaissance.

Our ambition is not just to make other worlds look closer. It is to make the process of preparing to explore them more transparent, rigorous, and accessible.

It provides access to the technical foundation behind NEXORA SPACE - ECHO-VOID ATLAS, including its interactive planetary exploration experience, terrain-analysis methodology, and ECHO virtual reconnaissance simulator.

Our goal is to make the project transparent, reproducible, and open to further development and collaboration
